pageCache.pageTitle: St John's CE Primary School | Crowborough, East Sussex
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St John’s CE Primary School
“Live life to the full” (John 10:10)
Our vision is to serve our school community by providing an education of the highest quality, that allows our children to flourish, within the context of Christian belief and practice. Our vision is underpinned by the bible verse “That they shall have life, life in all its fullness” (John 10:10).
‘Life in all its fullness’ means embracing an abundant, broad, deep rich sense of living together through all the ups and downs and twists and turns that life gives us. Our vision is what characterises children’s experiences of the life that we seek to offer them on a daily basis.
To live the life described in John 10:10 is a continual process or journey where we grow and flourish at different times in the trust that God has a plan for us. The children understand that ‘living life to the full’ is not just about all the fun things that happen at school, it is about everything that happens and how we learn to deal with it.
Our mission to “educate the heart, mind, body, and soul” refers to a holistic view of a person, encompassing their emotional (heart), intellectual (mind), physical (body), and spiritual (soul) characteristics, essentially meaning we consider everyone completely; not just in one dimension allowing them to flourish as an individual.
Relationships within the school are further developed by encouraging reflection, enquiry and a sense of ‘wonder’; additionally fostering our other core values of excellence, love and forgiveness. By following these core values, we can truly educate the mind, body, heart and soul of everyone here at St John’s.
St John’s is a unique school where we believe that there should be much more than academic rigor in the classroom. Whether it is playing together, caring for each other, (visit the Buddies section under the School Life link), taking part in sports or exploring creative talents, opportunities abound. We strive to maintain the right balance between enjoyment and achievement so that your child will thoroughly enjoy and benefit from their time here. High expectations are evident in all that we do and successes are celebrated.
St John’s is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and expects all staff, parents, governors and volunteers to share this commitment so that our pupils can thrive in a safe and caring environment.
Although the information available on this website gives you an insight into our life here at St John’s, a visit to the school is strongly recommended. We are confident that, after experiencing the warmth and happiness of the children and staff, you will leave convinced that St John’s has that something extra about it which is just right for your child.
If you wish to find out more about our school or if you would like a place for your child at our school please look at the Starting at St John’s page.
If you require a paper copy of any of the information documents in the Key Information section please call the school office who will be happy to help with your request.

Starting at St John’s
Welcome to St John’s CE Primary School!
It is hard to sum up exactly what makes St John’s a unique school but St John’s is a place where we believe that there should be much more than academic rigour in the classroom. Whether it is playing together, taking part in sports or exploring creative talents, opportunities abound. It is these extra opportunities which really encourage independence and responsibility within the children.
Another important aspect of the school is the caring and nurturing ethos which exists between staff and children and equally importantly between the children themselves. We strive to maintain the right balance between enjoyment and achievement so that your child will thoroughly enjoy and benefit from their time here.
The school gates are open from 8.40am each morning, with registration closing at 9am. The end of the day is 3.15pm for all classes.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reception Newsletters - St John's CE School, Crowborough
pageCache.text:
Reception Newsletters
A weekly newsletter will be published here on a Friday afternoon.
This provides information of our learning intentions each week, as well as providing essential reminders of what is happening in class.
Please see below. The newsletter is also posted on Tapestry each Friday.
This week our classroom was over taken by pirates! We have had lots of fun with some pirate themed learning. The children completed some super pirate writing as well as lots of adventure talk, creating and following maps to find treasure. We had a focus on junk modelling. As well as learning new ways to join materials together, children were encouraged to plan and evaluate their work, thinking about how we can improve our work by adding extra detail and decoration.
In R.E. we talked about how Christians believe that God created our beautiful world and that God trusts humans to take care of it. We wondered about how incredible it is that so many different animals and plants exist and we finished our ‘Earth from space’ pictures – the glitter came out!
It was another hot one, so lots of water play to stay cool and the water mister came out again. (We are enjoyng spraying the children way too much!) The playground was too hot and sunny for running games, so we did some ‘under the sea’ yoga in the classroom instead!
We have begun to talk about the transition to year 1 and have started a countdown on our classroom calander to the school holidays. As we go into next week we will be taking part in transition activities as well as free flow play between our classroom and the year 1 classroom. I hope that the the children will become excited about the prospect of moving on and up, as they begin to understand how they have grown way too big and clever now for reception!
I can’t believe next week will be my last full week with your wonderful children. I intend to enjoy every moment before the term comes to an end. Although sad to see them go, I cannot wait to watch them continue to flourish as they progress through the school.
Have a wonderful weekend,
Please do not hesitate to email me with any questions or queries: jbentley@stjohnsprimary.org

Governors
A warm welcome from the governors of St John’s CE Primary School.
The role of the Governing Body is to:
Day-to-day management of the school is the responsibility of the headteacher though some governors are allocated specific responsibilities by the Governing Body. Much of the work of the Governing Body is undertaken through meetings and regular visits to the school.
Our intent is that we are open and transparent in all that we do.
If there is anything that you would like to raise with the governors, whether you would like to discuss something directly or raise an item for consideration at one of our full governor meetings, you can contact us either by writing c/o the school, or by e-mail to our chair of governors:
Phil Morris – pmorris@stjohnsprimary.org
The governing board at St John’s Primary comprises of 13 positions. The majority of governors are appointed whilst the Headteacher and the Parish Priest, are ex-officio. Governors represent the views and positions of different bodies in relation to the school.

Parents
Parents are always welcome in the school
Our teachers are available at the end of the school day to talk over minor issues. If you wish to discuss anything for more than a few minutes then please speak directly to the teacher to arrange a mutually convenient time.
We welcome parent volunteers in the school and you can help in a number of ways, for example, listening to children read, assisting extra-curricular clubs and helping on school trips. We operate a text messaging service for parents so that we can keep parents updated and remind them about activities going on in the school. Please ensure that you notify the school if your mobile number changes.

Homework
We believe that homework can play an important part in the education of children.
An overwhelming number of our parents are in favour of their children having homework. We also recognise that homework is a voluntary activity and in order for it to work we rely completely on parental support.
We accept fully that parents with more than one child may not be able to spend as much time with each child on homework tasks but do expect each child to read with a parent at least 3 times a week. Such time as may be given is much appreciated but is completely at parental discretion.
Our homework policy recognises that family life comes before homework and families have different lifestyles. Many children have evening or weekend activities and time to relax is also important. The homework we set will help each child’s education but not at the expense of family life.
Our current homework guidelines are set out below. If you have any questions, suggestions or concerns, do please speak to your child’s teacher, the headteacher or email the school.

Welcome to the PTA page for St John’s Primary School
St John’s PTA are an important organisation within the St Johns School community. Our aims and objectives are:
To raise funds to help the school provide extra resources for the children by bringing together parents and teachers and working towards a common goal.
We also have a Facebook page – click here to visit our page.
Where the money we raise goes
Recently our fundraising focus has shifted to improving the outside play areas. Our aim is to create a new shaded area for the children and improve drainage so that these areas can be used all year round.
PTA funds also fund many regular school events:
Importantly the PTA also provides each class teacher with a £100 “extras” budget from which they can purchase whatever they like to enhance their classrooms throughout the year. Examples have included additional art and craft materials, project resources and wet play games.

We take pride in our school uniform and ask our parents to help us uphold our high standards by adopting the guidelines below.
Please ensure that all clothes are clearly named. Hair reaching shoulder length or longer should be neatly tied back. Stud earrings only which must be removed for PE.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - St John's CE School, Crowborough
pageCache.text:
Music
Music is a big part of life at St John’s
We have a large choir that meets each week and the whole school enjoys singing in assembly and across the curriculum.
We offer woodwind, string, guitar and piano/keyboard tuition provided by our East Sussex Music service: “Create Music” and many children also go to Area Music Centre activities or Summer schools. We also offer the chance to be part of a band with our “iRock” sessions.
Each child in Key Stage Two has a 45 minute lesson of curriculum music delivered by a specialist teacher every week, with children in EYFS and KS1 receiving a 45 minute lesson delivered by their class teacher in our well resourced music room. We follow the “Charanga” scheme for music teaching. There is also a dedicated music assembly for 20 minutes each week for the whole school. We have a well structured programme of listening music that runs across the year in every class. Children are also encouraged to take part in the many performance occasions, such as the Christmas Carol Service, Nativity and the Easter presentation. In the past few years, we have participated in many community events such as the Crowborough Civic Carol service, the Big Sing and Voice in a Million at Wembley.
Children are given opportunities to watch and listen to live music across the year with demonstrations from our visiting instrumental teachers, mini concerts and workshops, such as African drumming. Year 6 are lucky enough to be going to Glyndebourne in the Autumn to watch an opera!
Learning an instrument
Please click here for more information about Create Music (our county music hub) and the services they offer.
If you would like to learn an instrument, please email the School Office or directly apply using this link:
https://createmusic.org.uk/for-children-and-young-people/lessons-at-school/
You might like to watch this recruitment video featuring our very own pupils!
https://youtu.be/Sh34KoApf64
If you are interested in being in your own rock band, please pick up a leaflet from the school office or look at the website here:
https://irockschool.com/
